what: Death himself, the Grim Reaper who hunts the hero up out of the dungeon: a very tall, gaunt, terrible figure in a vast heavy black hooded robe, far grander than any lesser reaper. Inside the deep hood is a bare skull of chalk grey-white bone, never gold, large enough to read clearly, with two small points of cold white light deep in its black eye sockets and a closed lipless jaw. His two hands are bare bone, long finger bones with no flesh, chalk grey-white. On his belt hangs one large hourglass in a black iron frame. He has realistic proportions: a small skull, broad bony shoulders under the robe, very long arms, about eight heads tall.
colours: a heavy black robe with a broad border of tarnished silver embroidery at the hood, cuffs and hem, and one thin bright silver-white line of light along its whole right edge; a chalk grey-white skull and bone hands; cold white eye lights; a black iron hourglass with pale sand; a scythe with a long black shaft bound in silver rings and a huge curved blade of bright pale steel with a mirror-white edge.
wears: He wears one immense heavy black hooded robe that falls in deep heavy folds to the ground, whole and solid, its hem one clean edge with a broad silver border, never torn into wisps or smoke; the hood drawn far forward over the skull; a plain black belt with the hourglass hanging from it. No armour, no crown, no wings.
holds: He grips exactly one great scythe with both bone hands on its shaft, one hand high and one low, like a farmer about to mow: a long, thick, straight black shaft bound with silver rings, with one huge curved blade of bright pale steel fixed across its top end, the blade as long as his arm and drawn thick and bold. He holds nothing else: the hourglass hangs at his belt, not in his hand.
pose: He strides forward and to the left, one long leg stepping out from the robe, his body leaning into the stride, the scythe held slanting across his body in both hands with the great blade raised high above his hood on the left, ready to sweep down, his skull bent toward the viewer, the heavy robe swinging out behind him.
must_show: the Grim Reaper: a huge black hooded robe with a bare skull inside the hood
bone hands
one great scythe with a big bright steel blade, held high in both hands
silver embroidery and a lit silver edge so he reads on a dark floor
an hourglass at the belt
plainly grander and more imposing than the lesser death (a small ragged reaper with a plain iron scythe)

what: a deadite: an ordinary medieval villager's corpse raised and possessed by a demon from the Book of the Dead, a homage in costume only to the possessed dead of an old horror film. Every part of it is dead flesh, cold ash-grey, the dull grey of a wax candle gone cold, a colour no living person has, never blue, the face, neck, arms and hands alike. Its face is a possessed corpse's: two blank milky-white eyes with no pupils and no iris, the brightest things on its face, each ringed in dark grey, a wide unnatural grin stretched far too wide showing yellow-grey teeth, grey cracked skin, dark rings round the eyes, and long lank dark hair. It has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long thin limbs, about eight heads tall.
colours: cold ash-grey dead skin on every part, the grey of a cold wax candle, blank milky-white eyes in dark grey rings, yellow-grey teeth, lank black-brown hair, a dull dark grey-brown homespun tunic, the colour of wet peat and grave earth, nearly charcoal.
wears: It wears a medieval peasant's knee-length homespun tunic of dull dark grey-brown, the colour of wet peat, nearly charcoal, torn and grave-stained, a rope belt and rag leg-wrappings. Nothing else.
holds: Its hands are empty and it holds nothing; both grey hands are open with long dirty nails, the fingers hooked.
pose: Seen from the side, it lurches to the left on two legs, body twisted and pitched forward, head cocked sharply to one side with the wide grin turned toward the viewer, both arms reaching out ahead of it at different heights, the hooked grey hands clawing.
must_show: a possessed corpse: chalk-grey dead skin all over
blank milky-white eyes with no pupils
the wide unnatural grin
peasant's homespun tunic
both hands empty, reaching

Her skin is too pale, a cold sickly grey-white on her hands, arms and chin. She has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long limbs.

pose: She kneels on both knees on the ground, her body folded forward over her stomach as if in pain, both arms wrapped across her belly, her shoulders hunched and shuddering, her head hanging so low that the curtain of dark hair falls straight down over her whole face; she does not look up. long dark hair hanging over her whole face

what: a sorrowful, gentle ghost of the dungeon, a lost soul and not a monster: the see-through ghost of a middle-aged man in an old-fashioned long hooded robe, made entirely of pale ghost-light, every part the same pale colour like fog and old bone. His face is calm and sad, a living man's face with nose, lips and closed sad eyes, under the hood. The robe has no hem: from the waist down it narrows into one long tapering tail of mist that sweeps away behind him to the right and curls up at its tip like a comet's tail, so that he hangs in the air and nothing of him touches the ground. He has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long arms.

pose: He drifts in the air toward the viewer and a little to the left, his head bowed and tilted to one side in sorrow, both open hands held out low in front of him at different heights, the long tail of mist that is the lower half of his robe sweeping away behind him to the right.
must_show: a plainly ghostly figure: see-through, pale ash-white all over
a sad, gentle human face, not frightening
a hooded robe whose lower half is one tail of mist, floating
open empty hands held out, asking

His mail shirt is torn open at one shoulder and ragged at the hem. bare head, short beard, grieving face bowed
both hands on the pommel of a sword held point-down

what: the weeping ghost of a mother whose son was lost in the dungeon: the see-through ghost of a woman with long loose hair, made of pale ghost-light, her face, hair and hands pale ash-white like fog and old bone, her face gentle and wet with tears, eyes closed; the backdrop faintly shows through her and a faint glow lies along her edge. Her long gown is a second, darker ghost-colour, a cool slate grey like a rain cloud, loose and flowing, so that she is plainly clothed. weeping, a gentle sorrowful face
a darker ghost gown, modest
one small glowing gold locket

In the glow, filling most of the jar, is one small winged woman, a fairy as tall as a hand, standing pressed against the front of the glass with both palms flat on it, her face close to the glass looking out pleading. must_show: a broken clockwork knight-shaped automaton of dark bronze and iron
a bucket-shaped great helm with one glowing lens in the visor slit
the chest plate open, gears showing
sitting slumped, one hand held out asking

what: a small roadside memorial shrine left in a dungeon alcove by a grieving family: a stack of flat grey slate stones balanced one on top of another like a small tower, seven stones high, each a different size, the biggest at the bottom and the smallest on top, taller than it is wide, the edges of each stone catching the light. On the top stone stands one short white candle with one small yellow flame. Leaning upright against the foot of the stack is one small wooden toy sword, a child's toy with a broad flat blade, a short crossguard and a round knob on its hilt, as tall as half the stack. One square of cream paper with a child's simple drawing of a family is tucked between two of the stones, and a few gold coins lie on the bottom stone. There is no halo of glow around the flame.
colours: flat grey slate stones with pale lit edges and dark gaps between them, a pale brown wooden toy sword, cream paper with dark lines, bright gold coins, a white candle with a small yellow flame.
must_show: a tall stack of flat stones, a small stone tower
a toy wooden sword leaning against it
a lit candle on top
a child's drawing tucked in the stones, a few coins left as offerings

what: Celeste, a woman knight turned to stone by a basilisk: a life-size statue of a young woman in full armour, carved of dull dark weathered granite, the cold grey of a castle wall, rough and pitted and speckled with darker flecks, every part the same stone: her face, her hair, her armour, her cloak and her sword alike; it is stone and not skin, not metal and not marble. Her eyes are blank stone with no pupils. Her mouth is open wide in a scream, frozen. Thin dark cracks run across her. She has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall.
colours: dull dark weathered grey granite on every part, speckled and pitted, with black-grey shadows and a few pale grey worn edges, thin dark cracks; no other colour anywhere: no beige, no tan, no cream.
wears: She wears, carved in stone, a finely made suit of plate armour with a long tabard to the knees, all of it the same grey stone.
holds: Her right hand holds exactly one longsword, carved of the same grey stone, pointing down and back. Her left arm is flung up in front of her face, the palm out, to ward off what she saw. She holds nothing else.
pose: She is frozen mid-recoil, leaning back away from the left, her left arm thrown up before her face, her head turned aside with mouth open in a scream, her right hand with the stone sword low behind her, one foot stepping back.
must_show: a statue of a woman knight, every part dull grey stone, hair and face included
blank stone eyes, mouth open in a frozen scream
one arm flung up before the face
armour and a sword, all carved stone
